summary: Jan–May 2026 FFB was 9,458 t (6.44 t/ha): 18% below budget (7.88 t/ha) and 15% below last year (7.54 t/ha), as old plantings are in a low-crop phase.
Cost was RM281/t FFB against a RM310/t budget. General charges were 25% underspent and upkeep 24%, partly because manuring lagged.
Only 26 of 77 manuring rounds (34%) were done by May: Kieserite did not arrive until June and the estate is short of manurers.
The estate has 95 of 114 workers it needs, including 63 of 71 harvesters. Sprayers manage only 8 pumps a day against a potential of 12.
New pest pressure: bagworm at P15 (PA, June) and rat damage of 19% at PM20K in February (Agro). Both need follow-up census.

issues.title: Agronomy yield % changes miscalculated; Mar 2025 mean not reproducible
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Tables 16-17 divide the change by the NEW year's yield instead of the old one. Table 16 (2024 to 2025): PM20K 11.26 to 16.15 is shown as +30% but is +43%; PM15A 17.45 to 23.00 shown +24% but +32%; PM19J 15.50 to 16.72 shown +7% but +7.9%; mean 18.93 to 21.46 shown +12% but +13.4%. Table 17 (as at March, 2025 to 2026): PM05H 5.13 to 2.94 shown -74% but -43%; PM22L 0.27 to 1.59 shown +83% but +489%; PM15A 2.53 to 3.45 shown +27% but +36%; PM19J 4.25 to 3.40 shown -25% but -20%. Separately, the Table 17 mean for 2025 is printed as 4.20 t/ha, but the simple average of the ten block figures listed is 3.58 (the 2026 mean of 3.59 does reproduce). On the listed figures the estate mean is about flat (3.58 to 3.59), not down 17% (or 14.5%). The area-weighted means would be 3.33 and 3.54. Para 7.9 and the summary conclusion of a 17% decline rest on the 4.20 figure.

issues.title: Cost per tonne CPO column wrong in PA report
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 section 9: Harvesting & Collection actual is shown as RM634.21/t CPO, but RM864,891 / 1,723.76 t CPO = RM501.75, so the total of RM1,675.57 should be about RM1,543.10. The General Charges and Upkeep actual columns (468.97, 572.39) do equal RM / 1,723.76 t. The budget and annual columns for General Charges and Upkeep also divide by the actual to-date CPO (e.g. annual General Charges RM1,502.30 = RM2,589,611 / 1,723.76 t; the budget CPO is 1,743 t to date and 4,841.30 t annual, which would give RM534.90 annual). The Harvesting budget columns (930.05 and 2,232.10) imply about 1,310 t CPO, a third divisor. The RM/t FFB column is correct.

issues.title: Manuring progress described differently
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 (visit 20 Apr) says 2026 manuring followed the schedule with only minor delays, and that Mixture B is back on track. PA 1/2026 (visit 17 Jun) records only 26 of 77 rounds (34%) applied by May. Kieserite was scheduled for March but not delivered until June, and there was a labour shortage. Agro Table 6 (March) itself shows NK Mix 20%, Mixture B 24% and Ammonium Sulphate 0%.

issues.title: 2025 manuring called complete but CRF only 59%
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 says the 2025 programme was completed fully. Its own Table 5 shows CRF (replanting) at 4.62 of 7.86 t applied (59%) and ARP at 99%. The Executive Director had already queried this same 4.62 t CRF figure after Agro 2/2025.

issues.title: Area totals do not add up
issues.detail: Mature 1,469.53 + immature 495.47 + unplantable 4.92 = 1,969.92 ha. The PA area statement gives a total estate area of 1,965.00 ha, and Agro Table 1 gives a gross of 1,965.19 ha. Agro Table 2 totals 1,965.01 ha and shows PM20K as 101.59 ha against 101.58 elsewhere. In Agro Table 2 the PM15A phases (49.37 + 63.54 + 45.73 + 63.54 = 222.18 ha) do not add to the 214.28 ha total shown; PA gives A1 45.27 and A3 41.93 ha (sum 214.28).

issues.title: Palm census table internally inconsistent
issues.detail: In Agro 1/2026 Table 3, the previous palm counts add to 279,301 but the total is printed as 269,523. The 'current' total of 277,436 is +2.9% on the printed figure, yet the change is shown as -1%. PM95E is shown at 143 SPH both before and after, although its count changes from 26,682 (139.5 SPH on 191.32 ha) to 27,359. The report also says no recent census was done. The PA rat census lists PM95E at 186.59 ha against 191.32 ha in the area statement.

issues.title: Labour shortfall and ratio understated
issues.detail: In the PA 1/2026 labour statement, 95 workers are available against 114 required, a gap of 19, but the total variance is printed as -17 because the mandore gap of 2 is left out. The text says workers to planted ha is 1:18, but 1,965 ha / 95 = 1:20.7. The 1:18 figure matches the 1,702.23 ha harvesting area, not planted area.

issues.title: Rat baiting table uses wrong hectares
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 14 gives PR23B sub-blocks B2-B4 as 39.26, 62.33 and 55.04 ha. These are the PR24C C2-C4 areas; PR23B is 38.85, 76.10 and 61.51 ha in both its own Table 2 and the PA report. Palm counts also differ between reports, for example PM20K K1 at 7,031 palms (Agro) vs 6,550 (PA).

issues.title: Replanting timing conflict
issues.detail: The PA 1/2026 cover sheet records the Group MD's decision to defer replanting until 2029. Agro 1/2026 Table 4 tentatively schedules PM95 E5 & E6 for replanting in 2028, followed by E1 & E3 in 2029 and PM96F and PM97G in 2030.

issues.title: Fertiliser doses differ between PA schedule and Agro programme
issues.detail: For Mixture B round 1, the PA 1/2026 manuring table has P15 A3/A4 at 2.25 kg/palm and P19 J4 at 2.25 kg; Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1 has 2.00 kg for both. For round 2 the PA table has P20K at 1.75 kg against Agro's 2.00 kg. For rounds 1 and 2 the PA table has P21D at 1.50 kg against Agro's 1.75 kg.

issues.title: Bagworm status conflicts
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 (20 Apr) reports leaf-eating pests under control with no bagworm cases. PA 1/2026 (17 Jun) found a bagworm infestation at P15 and asked for an immediate census. This may be a new outbreak since April.

issues.title: Spraying programme areas inconsistent
issues.detail: The PA spraying tables split PM15A into 193.58 ha plus 20.70 ha (TR), while the PA area statement splits it into 158.58 ha plus 55.70 ha (TR). In the circle-spraying table, the year programmes for PM20K (304.74 ha) and PM21D (433.44 ha) equal 3 rounds, although the remarks say 4 rounds a year. The selective-spraying table uses 4 rounds.

actions.item: Recruit 8 harvesters, 5 sprayers and 4 manurers; bring worker ratio to 1:15 ha
Switch circle spraying to CDA or Inter Pump (GM to buy units, recover cost by instalments)
Raise mist-blower output from 8 to 12 pumps per man-day and enforce an 8-hour day
Start bagworm census at P15; spray Methamidophos above 10 active larvae per frond
Recheck and correct harvesters' outturn data
Rat damage census every 3 months; bait only above 10% damage
Consider wheelbarrows or semi-mechanised manuring to lift productivity
Complete 2,650 chains of road grading before the rainy season
Clarify with Head Office the missing running-cost budget for Hilux BRL8191
Spray circles and harvesters' paths in PR24C; eradicate Giant Paspalum
Carry out full palm census for all age categories; records outdated
Update rat and Ganoderma censuses; debole fallen Ganoderma palms
Improve frond stacking; keep fronds out of palm circles and paths
Control long stalks (cut under 5 cm) and unripe bunches through field pre-grading
Replace one circle-spray round with circle raking where debris is present; keep removing epiphytes in PM95E
Avoid over-pruning in newly mature PM22L

kb:
LADANG SUNGAI SISIK (slug sungai-sisek), owned by MUTIARA SUCI SDN BHD, Prosper group. Source reports: Planting Advisory (PA) Report 1/2026 by Mr. Boey Chee Weng (Planting Advisor), visit 17 June 2026, review period January to May 2026, figures as at May 2026. Agronomy Report 1/2026 by En. Alison Janari (Junior Agronomist) with Chong Kuan Ming (Senior Agronomist), visit 20 April 2026, figures mostly as at March 2026; previous agronomy visit 17 November 2025. General Manager Mr. Lee Chong Yew; Senior Manager En. Mohd Shafirun Bin Mohd Azba; Estate Manager En. Shukor Bin Yusoff (transferred in from Sg. Enggang Estate from February 2026, replacing Mr. Chan Wah Vee who went to Juasa Complex as Senior Manager).

AREA (PA, as at May 2026). Mature 1,469.53 ha: PM95E 191.32, PM96F 146.09, PM97G 74.46, PM05H 59.49, PM15A 158.58 plus PM15A TR 55.70, PM18I 129.10, PM19J 223.61 plus PM19J TR 1.80, PM20K 101.58, PM21D 144.48, PM22L 183.32. Immature 495.47 ha: PR23B 232.71, PR24C 196.69, PR25 (E2 and E4) 66.07. Unplantable 4.92 ha. Total estate stated as 1,965.00 ha (Agro gross 1,965.19 ha; the parts add to 1,969.92). Mature area rose from 1,286.21 ha to 1,469.53 ha as PR22L (183.32 ha) was declared mature in 2026. Immature fell from 612.72 to 495.47 ha. No replanting planned for 2026. Agro: mature 75 percent and immature 25 percent of planted area. 21 percent of palms are over 25 years old. Agro tentative replanting: 2028 PM95 E5 and E6; 2029 PM95 E1 and E3; 2030 PM96 F1-F3 and PM97G. The PA cover sheet records the Group MD's earlier decision to defer replanting to 2029.

PALM CENSUS (Agro Table 3). SPH: PM95E 143, PM96F 143, PM97G 148, PM05H 143, PM15A 121, PM18I 138, PM19J 141, PM20K 146, PM21D 148, PR22L 148. PR23B fell from 148 to 143 SPH (33,278 palms), PR24C from 148 to 143 (28,127 palms), and PR25 from 148 to 142 (9,382 palms). Total current 277,436 palms at 141 SPH. Agro says density records are outdated, no recent census has been done, and a full census of all ages is recommended.

LABOUR (PA, May 2026). Harvesters 63 vs 71 required (short 8). Drivers/loaders 5 vs 5. Weeders 21 vs 26 (short 5). Manurers 4 vs 8 (short 4). Mandore 0 vs 2. General workers 2 vs 2. Total 95 vs 114 required (April 90). Harvesters required at 1:24 ha on 1,702.23 ha under harvest, including scout harvesting in 2023 plantings; available ratio 1:27 ha. PA says worker ratio is 1:18 and should be 1:12 to 1:15. Main issues per PA: worker shortage and sprayer productivity.

STAFF (PA). Estate Manager Shukor Bin Yusoff; Assistant Managers Muhammad Faiz Bin Rosli (joined estate 9 Feb 2026, from Simpai 2) and Muhammad Nurhafizi Bin Zahari; Cadet Muhammad Zulhilmi Bin Hasmadi (joined Feb 2026); General Clerk Azura Binti Mardin; seven Field Conductors. Asst Mohd Dasuki resigned in January. Staff adequate.

CROP (PA, Jan to May 2026, on 1,469.53 ha). FFB 9,458.11 t vs budget 11,579 t; annual budget 32,264 t. Last year same period 9,702.76 t on 1,286.21 ha. CPO 1,723.76 t vs budget 1,743 t; kernel 472.92 t. OER 18.23 percent vs budget 15.05 (last year 15.66). KER 5.00 percent. FFB yield 6.44 t/ha vs budget 7.88 (18 percent below) and vs 7.54 last year (15 percent below); annual budget 21.96 t/ha. CPO yield 1.17 t/ha vs 1.19 budget. PA attributes the shortfall to late bunch ripening and the low-crop season in old plantings; only the 2020, 2021 and 2022 plantings had good fruit sets. Bunch weights May 2026 vs May 2025: 1995 21 vs 22 kg; 1996 22 vs 22; 1997 23 vs 23; 2005 21 vs 15; 2015 16 vs 15; 2018 13 vs 10; 2019 10 vs 9; 2020 8 vs 6; 2021 6 vs 4. PR23B scout harvesting began January, yielding 0.4 t/ha to May.

YIELD HISTORY (Agro Table 16, t/ha 2024 to 2025): PM95E 18.62 to 21.47; PM96F 20.62 to 23.66; PM97G 22.40 to 25.80; PM05H 24.16 to 29.81; PM15A 17.45 to 23.00; PM18I 21.44 to 25.31; PM19J 15.50 to 16.72; PM20K 11.26 to 16.15; PM21D 2025 11.24 (first year). Mean 18.93 to 21.46. Agro reports this as +12 percent; by the usual method (change divided by 2024) it is +13.4 percent. Agro percentages by block also divide by the 2025 figure, so by the usual method PM15A is +32 percent (shown 24), PM20K +43 (shown 30), PM05H +23 (shown 19), PM19J +7.9 (shown 7), PM95E to PM97G about +15 (shown 13). The means are simple averages of the block yields (2024 excludes PM21D). P22 immature yield in 2025 was under 2 t/ha, far below expectation. The estate managed nearly 23 harvesting rounds in 2025 against a minimum of 24. Agro links low 2025 yields partly to the drought in Q1 2024.
Jan to Mar yields (Agro Table 17, 'as at March', 2025 vs 2026, t/ha; the text calls it the first three months of 2026): PM95E 3.61 vs 4.16; PM96F 4.86 vs 4.60; PM97G 4.61 vs 3.90; PM05H 5.13 vs 2.94; PM15A 2.53 vs 3.45; PM18I 4.46 vs 4.42; PM19J 4.25 vs 3.40; PM20K 3.50 vs 4.24; PM21D 2.54 vs 3.23; PM22L 0.27 vs 1.59; printed mean 4.20 vs 3.59 (Agro says -17 percent). Agro's percentages divide by the 2026 figure. Correct changes by the usual method: PM05H -43 percent (not -74); PM22L +489 percent (not +83); PM15A +36 (not 27); PM19J -20 (not -25); PM97G -15 (not -18); PM20K +21 (not 17); PM21D +27 (not 21). DOUBTFUL FIGURE: the 2025 mean of 4.20 cannot be reproduced; the simple average of the ten block figures listed is 3.58 (2026: 3.59 matches), so on the listed block figures the estate mean is about flat, not down 17 percent. Area-weighted means would be 3.33 (2025) and 3.54 (2026). Dont quote a 17 percent or 14.5 percent decline for the estate mean without this caveat. The PA's estate-wide Jan to May 2026 yield of 6.44 t/ha vs 7.54 last year (-15 percent) is a separate, reliable comparison.

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA, RM per tonne FFB, to May 2026): General charges 85.47 vs budget 93.00; upkeep and cultivation 104.32 vs 111.84; harvesting and collection 91.44 vs 105.26; total 281.23 vs 310.10 (annual budget 268.61). PA rates cost as satisfactory. Per tonne CPO the PA prints a total of 1,675.57 vs budget 2,307.28. That column has errors: harvesting should be 501.75 (RM864,891 / 1,723.76 t CPO), giving a total of about 1,543.10.
General charges RM808,390.90 vs budget RM1,079,015 (annual RM2,589,611), 25 percent underspent. That is RM411.39/ha vs 549.12. Management and supervision RM367,430.61; labour and amenities RM182,654.89; other RM258,305.40.
Mature upkeep RM986,660 vs budget RM1,295,010 (annual RM3,107,963), 24 percent underspent. That is RM670.95/ha vs 880.64. RM/ha actual vs budget: weeding 104.09 vs 100.30; manuring 453.36 vs 650.83; pest and disease 9.76 vs 25.03; drains 38.14 vs 23.03; roads 19.29 vs 34.95; bridges 8.19 vs 8.07; pruning 38.12 vs 38.14. The manuring underspend reflects delayed fertiliser.
Harvesting and collection RM864,891 vs budget RM1,218,775: harvesting labour RM68.80/t vs 79.69, internal transport RM22.64/t vs 25.57.
Capital expenditure budget RM125,000 (residential buildings); nothing spent to May. Hilux BRL8191 ran 18,545 km at RM5,784 (RM0.31/km) with no budget; Head Office to be consulted.

FIELD UPKEEP (PA). Circle spraying: 1,740.68 ha (1.2 rounds) of 2,054.73 ha programmed (1.4 rounds), 85 percent. The shortfall is because Sg. Sisik workers were sent to help Simpai 2. Circles clean except P05. CKS high-volume spraying at 4.4 ha/man-day; piece rate RM17/ha; earnings RM74.80/day. Glyphosate at 0.23 l/ha (3.3 pumps/ha) is high. Only 8 pumps per man-day vs a potential of 12. Advised to use Inter Pump or CDA to reach 5 ha/man-day.
Selective spraying: 2,240.88 ha (1.5 rounds) of 2,939.06 ha (2 rounds), 76 percent. Mist blowers at 5.5 ha/man-day; RM17/ha; earnings RM93.50/day. Garlon 0.11 l/ha and Ally 0.04 kg/ha. Workers only work about 6.5 hours a day; 8 hours is required. Spots of woodies at P21, P05 and P19.
Agro (March) recorded spraying 100 percent on programme in mature blocks. It saw circle regrowth in PM95E, debris in circles (recommends one round of circle raking instead of spraying) and epiphytes in PM95E1 to E3. Nephrolepis should be kept as ground cover.
Manuring (PA): 26 of 77 rounds (34 percent) done to May. The cause is no Kieserite stock (scheduled March, delivered June) plus the labour shortage. Broadcasting output 23 bags/man-day at RM3.87/bag; earnings RM89.01/day. Advised to use wheelbarrows or semi-mechanisation. Agro (March) completion: NK Mix 58.15 of 295.31 t (20 percent); Mixture B 233.35 of 990.5 t (24 percent); Compound A 48.65 of 163.28 t (30 percent); Compound B 86.65 of 346.6 t (25 percent); AS 0 percent; RP 7.2 t (15 percent). Agro calls 2026 progress on schedule with minor delivery delays. P19J-2 application was checked at 30 bags/man-day with satisfactory quality; the store is acceptable. 2025 manuring: all items 100 percent except ARP 99 percent and CRF 4.62 of 7.86 t (59 percent).
Revised fertiliser programme (Agro Appendix 1, kg per palm): Old palms PM95E NK2 2.00 to 2.25 once, PM96F NK2 2.5 once, PM97G NK2 2.25 twice, PM05H Mix B 2.00 three times. Young mature: Mix B 1.75 to 2.25 twice, then Mix B 1.50 twice in the second half, with RP 1.5 to 2.0, AS 1.0 for P15 and P19 J1 to J3, and Kieserite 0.75 for P20 and P21 or 0.50 for P22. Immature: PR23B Compound 1.5 four times plus RP 2.0; PR24C Compound 1.0 twice and 1.2 twice plus RP 1.75; PR25 Compound 0.8 and 0.9 plus RP 1.5. The revision was driven by fertiliser pricing. Leaf sampling results will feed the 2027 programme.
Pruning: 7,347.65 ha (100 percent) progressively pruned and paid to May. Cost per ha per year: 1995 to 1997 RM140; 2005 RM120; 2015 to 2020 RM70; 2021 to 2022 RM60. Agro: pruning quality acceptable, but frond stacking inconsistent and fronds left in circles; avoid over-pruning PM22L.
Roads: none of the 2,650 chains of grading (RM19/chain) or 640 chains of laterite surfacing (RM105/chain) done to May; grading is to start in July. 600 t of crusher run (RM45/t) is on order. Drains desilted: 12x10x8 ft 729.84 of 804.45 chains (RM52); 8x6x4 ft 357.44 of 674.96 (RM46); 5x4x3 ft 502.65 of 910 (RM35).

HARVESTING (PA). 10 of 10 budgeted rounds done; average interval 14 days. The Group MD wanted intervals below 15 days and 2.5 rounds a month. Agro March intervals by field ranged from 9 to 20 days, with PM15A at 16 to 20 days. Harvester outturn data was wrong and must be corrected. Six mini tractors (4 cutters plus 1 collector) do in-field collection; wheelbarrows are used elsewhere. Rates per tonne and output (t/man-day): PM95E RM45 / 2.37; PM96F RM45 / 2.38; PM97G RM45 / 2.26; PM05H RM37 / 2.55; PM15A RM42 / 1.98; PM18I RM65 / 2.50; PM19J RM68 / 2.18; PM20K RM73 / 2.21; PM21D RM83 / 2.03; PM22L RM88 / 1.67; PR23B RM89 / 1.07. Basic wage RM65.39. Uncollected loose fruit was seen at P20/K2 (PA) and P95E-5 (Agro). Agro flags alarming numbers of long-stalk bunches and some unripe bunches; stalks should be under 5 cm.

PEST AND DISEASE. Rat damage (PA May table): PM05H 2 percent, PM15A 2, PM18I 5, PM19J 5, PM20K 3, PM21D 4, PR22L 2. Agro census: PM20K hit 19 percent in February 2026, above the 10 percent threshold; other young blocks were 2 to 5 percent. Baiting (PA): 2 rounds at J, 4 rounds at K, 3 rounds at D, and rounds in PR23B; no follow-up census done. Census every 3 months is required. Bagworm: PA found an infestation at P15 in June (census now; Methamidophos above 10 larvae per frond); Agro in April had seen none. Ganoderma insignificant (Agro); debole fallen palms. Mg deficiency at P95E-5 and PR23B (Agro). Oryctes in immature areas is sporadic after 10 rounds of Russel spraying (PA); Agro notes Russel Beta 2.9 EC at 50 ml per pump.

IMMATURE (PA, to May). PR23B (232.71 ha): upkeep RM158,312 vs RM288,545 budget (RM683/ha vs 1,245); cost from start RM1,414,285 upkeep plus RM1,868,709 development. Circle spraying 50 percent, selective 100 percent, fertiliser 2 of 2 rounds; 1,567 palms supplied by December 2025; basal pruning done January to March; scout harvesting 0.4 t/ha. PR24C (196.69 ha): upkeep RM177,776 vs RM244,395 (RM905/ha vs 1,241); circles 66 percent and due, paths grassy; selective 75 percent with Giant Paspalum; fertiliser 2 of 2 rounds; 2,686 palms supplied by November 2025. Agro (March) had PR24C circles at 72 percent and inter-row at 30 percent because of labour, with Mucuna encroaching. PR25 (66.07 ha): upkeep RM79,378 vs RM77,650 (over budget; drains RM7,811 vs RM625, supplying RM21,850 vs RM13,040); circles 100 percent, selective 67 percent, fertiliser 1 of 1 round; 750 palms supplied; development cost RM830,004 (RM12,555/ha).

RAINFALL (PA Appendix A). 2024: 2,241 mm over 115 days. 2025: 3,164 mm over 132 days. 2025 monthly mm: Jan 233, Feb 68, Mar 284, Apr 458, May 237, Jun 203, Jul 42, Aug 192, Sep 193, Oct 241, Nov 270, Dec 743.

PA CONCLUDING REMARKS: recruit harvesters, sprayers and manurers immediately; use CDA for circle spraying (the GM will buy units and recover cost by instalments); raise mist-blower pumps per day; consider semi-mechanised manuring; start bagworm census and spraying; keep replants well maintained. AGRO KEY POINTS: harvesting intervals inconsistent in Q1; yield in the first quarter down on 2025, mainly in old blocks; young blocks are trending up; full census needed; rat and Ganoderma census to be updated; fertiliser programme for the second half revised.

notes: Report names the estate Ladang Sungai Sisik (Mutiara Suci Sdn Bhd).

Report prints RM/ha (not RM/t) for general charges and upkeep items; RM/t computed as RM amount / FFB (actual 9,458.11 t; budget-todate 11,579 t), marked calc. Mature upkeep only (immature section excluded).
Group totals are as printed in section 9 and match the dashboard costParts.
General charges budget: printed 93.00, but RM1,079,015 / 11,579 t = 93.19 (items sum to 93.19).
Harvest items printed per tonne in section 7; they sum to the printed group totals (91.44 / 105.26). Harvesting labour and internal transport only.
